newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ air traffic controllers to strike for 3 hours.
newsitem.headline: NZ air traffic controllers to strike for 3 hours.

text.p: About 10,000 air passengers would have had to make some changes to their travel plans ahead of Monday's three-hour strike by air traffic controllers, the New Zealand Press Association reports.
Air traffic controllers are staging their third strike between 7 a.m. (1900 GMT) and 10 a.m. (2200 GMT) over pay and conditions and plan another strike at the same time on Friday.
Controllers staged two strikes in December for a total of seven days.
Air traffic controllers and their employers, Airways Corp, met under mediation in Christchurch on Friday. Both parties said the talks had been productive but the strike notices were not lifted.
Air NZ spokesman David Beatson said the airline did not expect any problems "providing we can all hit the strict time slots that we have been allocated correctly".
The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) approved contingency plan allows for a limited jet service in reserved airspace between Auckland, Wellington, Christchurch and Dunedin.
